title: Not Killing
note: This means not killing any living thing, from those with five senses to those with one, even by carelessness. It surpasses all the righteousness above and takes in what hasn’t been named, so it comes last.

couplets.plain: What is righteous action? Not killing. Killing brings with it every action of the other kind.
couplets.pm: If you ask what single action is all righteousness, it is killing nothing. Killing by itself yields all that sinful deeds yield: all the other sins together can’t bring the suffering that this sin brings. So not killing alone gives the fruit of all other righteousness.

links.quote: What is righteous action? Not killing
links.reason: Names not killing as righteous action itself, because killing brings every action of the other kind.

couplets.plain: Sharing your food and caring for many living things is first among everything the learned have gathered.
couplets.pm: Sharing what you eat with hungry beings and guarding all five kinds of life is the highest of all the righteous acts that writers on righteousness gathered for those who have renounced. Guarding means taking care that no killing happens even by carelessness, and sharing food is a necessary part of that. All the books agree on this.

links.reason: Makes sharing your food one half of the highest thing the learned have gathered.
Places caring for living things beside sharing food, first among all the learned have gathered.

couplets.plain: Not killing stands alone as good. Next after it, not lying is good.
couplets.pm: Among the righteous acts the books gather, not killing is good on its own, with no equal. Not lying is good standing behind it. This settles which ranks higher, since earlier couplets praised not lying so highly. Not lying comes second because a lie turns true when it brings good, and a truth turns false when it brings harm.

links.quote: Not killing stands alone as good
Next after it, not lying is good
links.reason: Honours not lying with the only place left, next after not killing.

couplets.plain: What is called the good path? The way that takes care to kill nothing at all.
couplets.pm: If you ask what is called the good path to the higher worlds and release, it is the way that means to keep the righteousness of killing no life at all. “Nothing at all” takes in even beings with one sense. Only a way that has this righteousness is the good way.

links.quote: takes care to kill nothing at all
links.reason: Measures the good path by its care to kill nothing at all.

couplets.plain: Among all who dread the state they are in and renounce, the highest is the one who dreads killing and keeps to not killing.
couplets.pm: Some fear the state of being born, in which every form of life, moving or still, has no joy and only suffering, and they leave household life so as not to be born again. Of all these, the highest is the one who fears the sin of killing and never forgets not to kill. Religions differ, so renouncers are many kinds.

links.quote: the highest is the one who dreads killing
links.reason: Ranks highest the renouncer who dreads killing and keeps to not killing.

links.quote: Among all who dread the state they are in and renounce

couplets.plain: Death, which eats lives, won’t come upon the days of someone who holds to not killing.
couplets.pm: Death, the eater of lives, won’t come upon the lifespan of someone who keeps not killing as a vow. The greatest righteousness bears fruit in this very life, so such a person isn’t killed and lives out the span set for them. Time stretches out, wisdom is born and the soul gains release.

links.quote: someone who holds to not killing
links.reason: Holds out the rarest reward for not killing: days that death leaves alone.
Death is an eater of lives who won’t come upon this person’s days.

couplets.plain: Even if you lose your own life for it, don’t do what takes another sweet life.
couplets.pm: Even if your own life leaves your body for refusing, don’t do the deed that takes another sweet life from its body. Let it kill you rather than kill it, because sin wears away in the one killed and grows in the one who kills. He rejects the reading that this means a life lost for want of a propitiatory rite, since others may not do such killing either.
couplets.sensitive: counsels dying rather than killing, even to survive

links.quote: Even if you lose your own life for it

couplets.plain: Even if the gain is great and good, to the worthy, gain that comes from killing is the lowest thing.
couplets.pm: Householders are told that killing in sacrifice for the gods brings great wealth full of joy. Even so, for those made complete by renunciation, wealth got by killing a life is the lowest. That wealth is becoming a god in heaven, which is small and leads to rebirth, beside the endless joy of release. Killing may reach heaven, but not release.

links.quote: gain that comes from killing is the lowest thing
links.reason: Rejects any gain won by killing, however great it may be.

couplets.plain: People who live by killing are, in the minds of those who can see baseness, doing unclean work.
couplets.pm: Those whose work is killing don’t see how base it is, but in the minds of those who do, they are low-caste by their work. Saying “whose work is killing” shows that killing in sacrifice isn’t meant. They fall to this lowness in this very life.
couplets.sensitive: the Tamil ranks killers with low-caste work

links.reason: Shows the contempt a living made by killing earns from those who can see baseness.

couplets.plain: They say that those living a poor, wretched life in diseased bodies are those who took life from bodies.
couplets.pm: Some have bodies too diseased to look at and live in poverty at low work. Those who know how deeds ripen say these people took lives from their bodies in an earlier birth. So killers receive this too in the life to come, and disease such as leprosy is part of it.
couplets.sensitive: blames the sick for their disease

links.quote: are those who took life from bodies
links.reason: Has people trace a diseased body to lives taken before, a deed coming home in the flesh.
Reads a diseased body as the price of taking life, which warns against it.
